data.risk: Hartford H1-2026 overall 5.0/10 (higher = riskier; sovereign 8.5, war on land 5.0) vs Saudi 3.5. Coface C (June 2026), expects sharp 2026 contraction. Hormuz still disrupted (12 ship attacks 28 Sep–7 Oct 2026); Khalifa Bin Salman Port was suspended in March; Bahrain ~92% import-dependent and supplied overland via King Fahd Causeway. Use advance payment or confirmed L/C for new buyers.
data.scoreBasis: Small market (1.6M pop, ~$49B GDP) but Egypt is #1 supplier of HS1806 (12.7%, 2023) and #8 in HS2106; GAFTA 0% duty. War-driven Hormuz disruption makes Saudi overland supply the main route, which favours Dr. Baker's Madinah plant. Risk higher than Saudi (Hartford 5.0 vs 3.5). Clear B2B channel exists (HHM's Advanced Bakery Solutions, Fine Foods) plus local users (Amalfi Foods, Tariq Pastries). Main competitors: Almarai, Al Alali, SwissBake/Puratos.
data.tariffNote: GAFTA: Egyptian-origin goods 0% with Arab certificate of origin (vs GCC CET 5% CIF). Goods from the Madinah plant can enter as GCC national products (40% value added, 51% GCC ownership, GCC certificate of origin). VAT 10%; basic dairy zero-rated (list of 118 items, Sep 2024).
